record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Does there exist a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph? Here a 5-graph is a 5-regular graph in which every odd vertex set X has at least 5 edges to its complement, and poorly matchable means that any two perfect matchings intersect.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2 Is there a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a 5-graph to be a 5-regular multigraph G such that for every vertex subset X ⊆ V(G) of odd cardinality, the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in X is at least 5. A graph is called poorly matchable if it has at least one perfect matching and any two perfect matchings of it share at least one edge. The graph G is said to be 5-edge-connected if removing fewer than 5 edges leaves it connected.

Question: Does there exist a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on poorly matchable r-graphs indicates that no 5-edge-connected poorly matchable 5-graph is known; all known poorly matchable r-graphs contain a 4-edge-cut. The question is explicitly raised as open, and related work (e.g., Thomassen's conjecture and results on pairwise disjoint perfect matchings in r-edge-connected r-regular graphs) leaves it unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The hardness of recognising poorly matchable graphs and the hunting of the d-snark
status_evidence.snippet: All known poorly matchable r-graphs have a 4-edge-cut; no 5-edge-connected poorly matchable 5-graph is known.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph is open.

status_evidence.title: Edge-Connectivity and Pairwise Disjoint Perfect Matchings in Regular Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies pairwise disjoint perfect matchings in r-edge-connected r-regular graphs; high edge-connectivity may force disjoint perfect matchings.
status_evidence.claim: The closely related question of whether high edge-connectivity forces disjoint perfect matchings in r-graphs remains an active area.
